title: MNIST
blurb: The most famous handwriting in machine learning: 300 digits from the MNIST test set, 30 of each. Pixels versus DINOv2, a vision model that never saw a digit in training.

notes.rsa: Almost no agreement. In pixel space two digits are close only when their ink lands on the same squares; DINOv2, trained on photos, is looking at something else entirely: stroke weight, slant, overall blobness.

about.name: THE MNIST DATABASE of handwritten digits
about.quote: The MNIST database of handwritten digits, available from this page, has a training set of 60,000 examples, and a test set of 10,000 examples. It is a subset of a larger set available from NIST.
